passage: Water is a precious resource, yet many people mistakenly believe that rain refills our supplies instantly, making conservation unnecessary. In reality, fresh water is limited and unevenly distributed across India, with some regions receiving heavy rainfall while others face severe scarcity. Much of our water comes from groundwater stored in underground layers called aquifers. When we pump water from these aquifers faster than rain can soak into the ground to replenish them, the water table drops significantly. If a borewell runs dry, it does not mean the water is gone forever, but it does mean we have exhausted the local supply at that depth. To manage this, we must adopt smart habits. For instance, water used for washing vegetables or clothes is not useless; it can be reused for watering plants or cleaning floors. Furthermore, rainwater harvesting is not just for places with heavy rain; it is a vital method to capture runoff and direct it into the ground to recharge aquifers, rather than letting it evaporate or flow away. Even small actions, like turning off the tap while brushing, prevent the waste of treated water. Saving water is a shared responsibility for everyone, including students, because every drop we save helps maintain the balance of our local water cycle.

items.evidence: When we pump water from these aquifers faster than rain can soak into the ground to replenish them, the water table drops significantly.
items.q: A village pumps groundwater faster than rain can soak in. What happens to its water table?
options: It falls lower as water is used up
It stays level because groundwater refills quickly
It rises because pumping pulls water upward
It stays level because rain refills it instantly
items.explain: Pumping faster than rain can soak in makes the water table drop.

wrong.why: thinks groundwater refills as fast as it is pumped

items.evidence: If a borewell runs dry, it does not mean the water is gone forever, but it does mean we have exhausted the local supply at that depth.
items.q: Meena's borewell has run dry. What does this tell us about the water below?
options: The water at that depth is used up
The water below is gone for good
The water below can never truly run out
The water will come back after one rain
items.explain: A dry borewell means the local supply at that depth is exhausted, not gone forever.

wrong.why: thinks a dry borewell means no water anywhere below
thinks groundwater can never run out
thinks rain refills water at once

items.evidence: For instance, water used for washing vegetables or clothes is not useless; it can be reused for watering plants or cleaning floors.
items.q: Which is the best way to use water left after washing vegetables?
options: Pour it on the plants in the garden
Pour it away, as used water is useless
Pour it away, as it returns to nature
Pour it away, as rain will refill supplies
items.explain: Water used for washing vegetables is not useless; it can water plants or clean floors.

wrong.why: thinks used water has no further use
thinks water down the drain is not wasted
thinks rain makes saving water unnecessary

options: Yes, it sends runoff into the ground
No, it only works where rain is heavy
